content: Your doctor has prescribed the medication Mesna to assist in the treatment of your condition. Mesna can be administered either as an injection into a vein or taken orally by mixing the liquid with juice. Depending on your chemotherapy schedule, Mesna will be given before and after each dose of chemotherapy or combined in the same infusion bag with your chemotherapy drugs. This medication is specifically used to protect the bladder lining from the harmful effects of certain cancer-fighting drugs. Precautions Before Taking Mesna: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to Mesna or any other medications. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a list of all prescription and non-prescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins and supplements. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It is advised not to plan for pregnancy while undergoing chemotherapy or for a period after completing treatment. Discuss further details with your doctor. Use a reliable form of birth control to prevent pregnancy during treatment. Do not receive any live vaccines (e.g., measles or flu shots) without consulting your doctor. Side Effects: Minor Side Effects: Common side effects of Mesna include: An unpleasant taste in the mouth Diarrhea or soft stools Headache Nausea Vomiting If you experience severe or prolonged fatigue, inform your doctor. Severe Side Effects: If you notice blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. For any serious side effects, you or your doctor may report them to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. In Case of Emergency or Overdose: If an overdose occurs, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911.
